mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60d returns in more than 60% of quarters with GDPC1 YoY decline < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20d returns in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE > 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO and a fall in HOUST over two months indicates supply-side inflation with weakening housing demand, which erodes corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0% MoM and HOUST < 0% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a surge in household savings, reflecting precautionary behavior and lower consumption, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60d returns in more than 60% of episodes where RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average by >10%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS and a decrease in UNRATE over two months indicates job creation without wage growth, suggesting inflationary pressure is contained, which supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0% MoM and UNRATE < 0% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent FEDFUNDS rate below 2% for more than one year signals an extended easing cycle, which lowers borrowing costs and supports corporate investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of extended FEDFUNDS < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in GDPC1 and INDPRO above their 12-month moving averages signals synchronized growth in output and industrial production, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-mo MA and INDPRO > 12-mo MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when both GDPC1 and INDPRO exceed their 12-month moving averages.
